newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: UBS enters debate on Philippine banks, says sell.
newsitem.headline: UBS enters debate on Philippine banks, says sell.

text.p: Swiss-based UBS Global Research added its voice to a debate over high-flying Philippine banking shares on Monday with a recommendation to sell.
The broker, a subsidiary of Union Bank of Switzerland, has recommended a sell on Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co Inc (Metrobank), Philippine National Bank (PNB) and Security Bank Corp.
The firm also told investors to avoid Union Bank of the Philippines.
In a research paper made available to Reuters on Monday, UBS rated Bank of the Philippine Islands and Philippine Commercial International Bank (PCIBank) as "hold".
Other brokerages, however, have suggested that Philippine banks are still the best buys.

"Banks are riding on the boom of the economy. There's no other sector which has benefited more on a surging economy except the banking sector," Rachel Evangelista, analyst at All Asia Capital, said in early February.
Brokerage Urbancorp Securities recommended subscribing to Equitable Banking Corp, the latest commercial bank to sell part of its shares to the public.

But UBS analyst Carlos Jalandoni said mounting competition in the industry will limit the sector's growth potential, prompting some banks to take on high-risk loans to offset the thinning margins in traditional loans.
The banking and financials sub-index has been outperforming the overall market since the start of the year, rising 11.7 percent against 4.1 percent for the composite index.
Major local banks enjoyed double-digit net profit growth last year and are forecast to grow by another 20 to 25 percent in 1997.
Jalandoni said the sector was bound for a consolidation. He said local banks faced aggressive foreign competitors as well a shortage of skilled workers.
He said asset quality would become a major concern this year because of significant exposure to real estate and foreign exchange loans.

"While the sector consolidates, we advise investors to sell into strength ... the Philippine banking sector currently trades at 18.2 times 1997 estimated earnings, a premium to the market's 17.5 times. We advise investors to underweight the sector by at least 30 percent," Jalandoni said.

But on Monday, the market continued to favour banking stocks. PNB gained five pesos to 310 ($11.76), while BPI added two pesos to close at 190. Metrobank was unchanged at 730 pesos and Security Bank was steady at 55 pesos.
On the other hand, UnionBank slid one peso to 30 pesos, while PCIBank fell 7.50 pesos to 385.
"Everybody is waiting for the banking issues to correct, but nobody is willing to sell," Noel Reyes, Anscor-Hagedorn Securities vice-president for research, said.
He said the sector is vulnerable to profit taking, but said earning prospects remained strong despite competition.
